title.rendered: Be Still and Know: Rest as Our Confession of Who God Is | Living from Rest, Day 9

excerpt.rendered: Psalm 46:10 is a battlefield command: cease striving, and know that I am God. Day 9 of Living from Rest explores what our stillness actually confesses.

content.rendered:
Be still is not a yoga mat verse. It is a command from the middle of a shaken world. Our stillness is a confession: He is God, and we are not.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, November 9, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 9

Today’s Scripture

“Be still, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth! The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.”
Psalm 46:10-11 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Psalm 46 is the psalm that sits behind Martin Luther’s hymn “A Mighty Fortress Is Our God.” It is not written for a quiet retreat; it is written for a shaken world. Verse 2 says, “Therefore we will not fear, even though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea.” This psalm belongs on the news cycle, not just the pillow.

And right at the climax of the psalm, in verse 10, God Himself speaks: “Be still, and know that I am God.” The NKJV says that. The AMPC says, “Let be and be still, and know (recognize and understand) that I am God.” The TPT says, “Surrender your anxiety! Be silent and stop your striving and you will see that I am God.” The Hebrew verb for “be still” is raphah, which carries the sense of letting go, dropping your hands, ceasing to strive.

Three things to notice. First, the command is to stop. Stop the frantic self-rescue. Stop the striving. Stop the panicked chatter in your own head. Second, the command is to know. Rest is not an escape from reality; it is a deeper confession of reality. God is God. He is still on the throne. He is still over the nations. Third, the command is to see Him exalted. Your stillness is not a disappearance; it is the backdrop against which God Himself will be glorified.

So when you are still, you are preaching. Your stillness announces something about God. It says: He does not need my panic to run the universe. He does not need my clenched fist to steady the earth. The God of Jacob is our refuge. The Lord of hosts is with us. Our stillness is confession, not escape.

If the news is loud, if your home is loud, if your own mind is loud, Psalm 46 is for you. Be still. Not because the storm is gone. Be still, because the God in the middle of the storm has told you to. Let go. Drop your hands. Know. “The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.”

What Stillness Confesses

God is God. You are not the ultimate solution to anything.

God is here. The Lord of hosts is with us.

God is enough. The God of Jacob is our refuge.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You that You are God and that You are with me. Thank You that the Lord of hosts is with me and the God of Jacob is my refuge, just as You said in Psalm 46:11. I drop my hands and I rest in what You have already done. I am not shaken, because You cannot be shaken. You are exalted among the nations, exalted in the earth, and exalted over my day. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
